judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Indicators (same grain) under the same Content Standard B4.3.3.2 'Demonstrate an understanding of area of regular and irregular 2-D shapes' in Sub-Strand 'Measurement- (Perimeter and Area)', and both carry the resolved Grade coordinate BASIC 4 (rank 0). B4.3.3.2.2 (second) covers selecting and justifying referents for the square units cm² and m² (LCs: 'Select referents for the units cm² or m²', 'Justify referents for the units cm² or m²'); B4.3.3.2.4 (first) covers developing and applying a formula for the area of a rectangle and square (LCs: 'Develop a formula...', 'Apply a formula...'). These are substantively coherent, complementary components of measuring area in square units — unit referents give meaning to the cm²/m² in which formula-derived areas are expressed — which is more than generic repetition or reusable LC overlap. However, the evidence does not support a developmental dependency at equal rank: referent selection/justification is a benchmark-and-estimation skill whose visible in-standard target is the sibling indicator B4.3.3.2.3 ('Estimate area by using referents for cm2 or m2', seen in the retained source_context_labels), while formula development rests on unit-square/array reasoning (B4.3.3.2.1 'Recognise that area is measured in square units'). The remaining nomination signals (shared ancestors, shared tag 'area', stop-word token/trigram overlap, weak code prefix, weak page proximity) are explicitly weak or generic and cannot by themselves license buildsTowards in either direction. Canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction is therefore the supported judgment; endpoint order is technical only. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all endpoints/ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, which is retained and did not alter this judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same rank 1) within the Number strand's operations area. B5.1.2.1.1 develops mental strategies and number properties to recall basic multiplication facts to 81 and the related division facts; B5.1.2.4.1 requires dividing 3-digit numbers by a 1-digit number 'efficiently' (its Content Standard parent B5.1.2.4 concerns understanding division of 2- or 3-digit numbers). Fluent recall of basic division/multiplication facts is the substantive sub-skill that makes efficient multi-digit division procedures feasible, so proficiency in the fact-level indicator supports success in the multi-digit division indicator rather than the reverse; this is pair-specific skill dependency, not mere shared 'number' wording or code prefix. Direction at equal rank is justified by the fact-level-to-algorithmic-application progression. Evidence is limited: both endpoints and their parents carry unresolved ancestry (framework-root fallback not used as placement evidence), source evidence is truncated, and the first endpoint carries a same-code/different-content audit flag for B5.1.2.1.1; the genuine Number Operations mental-math occurrence (window 174) is the text used here, matching the second endpoint's window 174 source context.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 5 Indicators (same statement-type grain, same canonical rank 1) under Content Standard B5.1.1.3 on factors and multiples of numbers 1-100. The first (B5.1.1.3.1) asks learners to identify the factors of whole numbers 1-100; the second (B5.1.1.3.4, LC tags 'hcf', 'prime factors') asks them to determine the highest common factor of 2 or 3 numbers by prime factorisation. Determining HCF requires the more complex combination of factor identification across multiple numbers plus prime-factor decomposition, so fluency in identifying factors substantively supports success with prime factorisation and HCF; the reverse direction is not supported. This is pair-specific skill extension, not mere shared-parent or code-prefix proximity. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream merge/audit context, but the retained statement texts and LCs are sufficient and mutually consistent.

judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 6 Indicators (rank 2, same Grade coordinate) under Strand 2: Algebra, but in different Sub-Strands: B6.2.1.1.7 ('Write a rule in words and in algebra to represent a given pattern', Sub-Strand 1 Pattern and Relationships, LCs for rule-in-words and rule-in-algebra) and B6.2.2.1.1 ('Demonstrate understanding of algebraic expressions as mathematical phrases that can contain letters which represent ordinary numbers and operators', Sub-Strand 2 Algebraic Expressions). They share substantive conceptual coherence: symbolic representation in which letters stand for numbers is exactly what is used when a pattern rule is expressed in algebra, so the two mutually reinforce symbolic-algebra understanding. Shared Strand/Grade ancestry, weak code-prefix and page proximity, and the single shared token 'represent' are nomination signals only, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits exemplar-level confirmation of dependency.
